parsed.study_design: Comparative case-based narrative synthesis combining literature review with the authors’ detailed groundwater studies and field experience
parsed.population_and_sample: Groundwater-dependent rural settlements, farmers, landholders and landless people across Indian aquifer settings, with detailed cases from Mehsana, Gujarat, and Pabal and other sites in Maharashtra; no fixed participant sample reported
parsed.exposure: Land-linked groundwater rights and weak regulation, interacting with aquifer characteristics, landownership, institutional arrangements, groundwater markets and unequal capacity to invest in wells and pumping technology
parsed.outcome: Groundwater access, availability and exclusion, including loss of access as aquifers decline, unequal shares of water, vulnerability of public drinking-water supplies and affordability-related barriers to continued extraction
parsed.rationale: The methods description states that the research combines a groundwater literature study with the authors’ own experience and detailed studies from different parts of India (p. 994, “Locating groundwater competition”). Empirical case evidence from Mehsana and Pabal documents changes in wells, groundwater levels, extraction practices and unequal access, while the outcomes section links markets, institutions, landholding and investment capacity to access and exclusion (pp. 997–1007). The paper therefore supplies empirical comparative evidence relevant to household/community drinking-water access as well as irrigation, rather than only offering doctrinal or normative commentary.
